habit_scope: AF&PA Exterior Siding and Coverings: wood/hardboard siding over Type 15 felt on 1–2 story wood-frame. Masonry veneer and wood shingles as wall covering are variants in this same chapter, not separate Methods. Roof-finish asphalt shingles are not this chapter.
how_it_is_done: Paper is already on (m-P10-sheathing-paper). Siding and exterior trim go over Type 15 asphalt felt or other water-repellent sheathing cover with corrosion-resistant nails — hot-dipped galvanized steel, stainless steel, or aluminum (AF&PA Wood Siding).
Keep all siding types ≥6 in above finished grade (AF&PA Exterior Siding; Fig 54). Same 6-in siding-to-grade already named in the termite chapter.

Smooth-shank siding nails: length = siding thickness + sheathing thickness + 1½ in penetration into solid wood. Foam or insulation-board sheathing: that 1½ in is into the stud. Plywood / wafer-board / OSB thickness counts toward the 1½ in. Ring-shank or spiral-shank may reduce required solid-wood penetration by 1/8 to 1/4 in. Extra foam-sheathing rules point to AF&PA appendix Item 9 — not printed here; do not invent them.
Bevel siding and square-edged boards horizontal: one nail at each stud. Minimum lap 1 in. Nail about 1½ in above the lap (Fig 68(a)).
Drop and shiplap (flush to the paper): one nail at each stud about 1½ in above the drip edge. Two nails if the siding is 8 in or wider, or if sheathing is omitted (Fig 68(b)).

Vertical board (square-edge or T&G, board-and-batten, board-on-board): if wood / plywood / structural panel sheathing is ≥½ in, nails 16 in vertically. Other sheathing: 1x4 furring at 24 in as a nail base. If studs exceed 16 in, 2-in lumber blocking between studs (Figs 68(c)(d)).

Corner boards, mitered corners, metal corner covers, or alternately lapped corners — house design (Fig 69). Ends at corners, butts, and window/door trim get clear water-repellent preservative before caulk and paint. If the siding weathers unfinished, a liberal coat on the whole surface (Protection of Siding).

Wood shingles/shakes as wall covering: weather exposures Table II (not invented here). Corrosion-resistant nails long enough to penetrate wood sheathing. Two nails up to 8 in width; three if wider. Single course: nails 1 in above the next course’s butt. Non-wood sheathing: 1x3 furring at the weather-exposure spacing (Fig 55).

Masonry veneer on wood frame sits on the masonry foundation wall. On PWF: on the treated footing plate or a treated knee wall, corrosion-resistant metal ties at 24 in o.c., each tie supporting no more than 2 sf, fastened through sheathing to foundation studs (Fig 70). PWF veneer: 1-in space between sheathing and masonry; base flashing from the outside face of the masonry over the foundation and up the sheathing ≥12 in; weep holes = open vertical joints at 4-ft intervals in the bottom course. Do not copy that PWF flashing paragraph onto a CIP/CMU veneer as if the book printed it there.

This phase can overlap P12 MEP rough and P14 drywall on the spine (can_overlap stub). AF&PA does not print lag days — do not invent them. Roof-finish asphalt shingles are not this chapter (roof sheathing / spaced sheathing lives in P09 leftover).
can_overlap_notes: Spine stub: cladding can overlap MEP rough and drywall. No lag_days. AF&PA does not print a lag.

inspection_hold_points: Siding over Type 15 felt / water-repellent cover (Wood Siding).
Bevel: min 1 in lap; nail ~1½ in above the lap, one nail per stud (Fig 68(a)).
Smooth-shank: 1½ in into solid wood (stud if foam sheathing; plywood/OSB counts).
PWF masonry veneer only: 1-in cavity, base flashing ≥12 in up the sheathing, weeps at 4 ft in the bottom course (Fig 70).
when_this_beats_habit: This is the AF&PA wood-siding habit. Masonry veneer and shingle walls are variants in the same chapter, not competing Methods from this set.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Nailing bevel siding through the lap (book puts the nail 1½ in above the lap). Skipping the 6-in grade clearance. Copying PWF veneer flashing onto a CIP/CMU veneer as if it were printed there. Inventing an asphalt-shingle roof-finish sequence from this chapter.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They hang siding. What they skip is 1½ in solid-wood penetration, 1 in min bevel lap, and 6 in off grade as printed.
permit_gate: cladding type should show on drawings; not a foundation-type swap
permit_gate_notes: Siding vs veneer vs shingle wall is a finish choice on the drawings. Confirm with AHJ. WUI is Fontana foothills only (mn-fontana) — not this Method.
risk_if_swapped_late: Paper is already under the siding. Swapping siding type after it is on is a finish tear-off. Book did not name dollars.
plain_language_summary: On the 2-story stick house the wood siding goes over the paper, at least 6 inches off the dirt. Bevel siding laps 1 inch minimum and gets one nail per stud about 1½ inches above that lap — not through the lap. Nails have to get 1½ inches into solid wood (the stud, if the sheathing is foam). This work can overlap MEP rough and drywall. No lag days invented. Roof shingles are not this chapter.
spanish_summary: En la casa de 2 pisos la madera va sobre el papel, a 6 pulgadas del suelo. El biselado traslapa 1 pulgada mínimo y lleva un clavo por poste a 1½ pulgadas arriba del traslape. El clavo entra 1½ pulgadas en madera sólida (el poste si el forro es foam). Puede traslaparse con el rough de MEP y el drywall. Sin días de espera inventados. Las tejas de techo no son este capítulo.
